subject: Change the order how ggplot draws border colors in geom_bar

messages.author: 3afef93b5704ceff
messages.subject: Change the order how ggplot draws border colors in geom_bar
parts:
Hi,

this was unanswered at SO, but i really would like to solve it.

https://stackoverflow.com/questions/50234274/change-the-order-how-ggplot-draws-border-colors-in-geom-bar

df <- data.frame(Taxon=c("A", "B", "C"),
                     Counts=c(0.1,0.5,0.4),
                     Treatment=rep("X1",3),
                     Effect=factor(c("A","B","A")))
    df$Effect <- factor(df$Effect, levels=c("A","B"), ordered=T)
   
    ggplot() +
      geom_bar(data=df, aes(x = Treatment, y = Counts, fill = Taxon, colour=Effect),
               stat="identity", position="fill", width=0.5)+
      scale_fill_manual("",values=c("gold", "green","yellow"))+
      scale_color_manual("",values=c("black","red"))

i want to highlight the effect "B" with a red border around all "Taxon" of that effect type. But ggplot seems to draw the rectangles in sequential order of `df$Taxon`, and not as i would wish by first applying the color assigned to df$Effect == A, then df$Effect == B. The same is true when changing the order of df$Effect.

    df$Effect <- factor(df$Effect, levels=c("B","A"), ordered=T)
   
   
    ggplot() +
      geom_bar(data=df, aes(x = Treatment, y = Counts, fill = Taxon, colour=Effect),
               stat="identity", position="fill", width=0.5)+
      scale_fill_manual("",values=c("gold", "green","yellow"))+
      scale_color_manual("",values=c("black","red"))

How to code this when i want to always have complete red rectangles around taxons expressing the effect "B"?

messages.author: 942ffec526d6a312
messages.subject: Re: Change the order how ggplot draws border colors in geom_bar
parts:
Hi,

> this was unanswered at SO, but i really would like to solve it.
>
> https://stackoverflow.com/questions/50234274/change-the-order-how-ggplot-draws-border-colors-in-geom-bar

For geom_point, I'd just suggest reordering the data.frame so
that the bits you wanted to be plotted last (Taxon B) are drawn
last. But that doesn't seem to apply to geom_bar: it is dependent on
factor level order which would mean that Taxon levels in the factor
would need to be c("A","C","B") which might not be desirable and
I believe would put B at the top all the time.

So this idea is a bit of a kludge, drawing the bar twice but with only
the red outline second time around.

> df <- data.frame(Taxon=c("A", "B", "C"),
>                      Counts=c(0.1,0.5,0.4),
>                      Treatment=rep("X1",3),
>                      Effect=factor(c("A","B","A")))
>     df$Effect <- factor(df$Effect, levels=c("A","B"), ordered=T)

You shouldn't really use df as a data.frame name since there is
a function df (the density function for the F distribution).

You don't need Effect for my solution (I couldn't get variations
on your code to work) - you can handle it in the scale_fill_manual.

So:

DF <- data.frame(Taxon = c("A", "B", "C"),

stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

ggplot(DF,aes(x = Treatment, y = Counts)) +
geom_bar(aes(fill=Taxon), stat='identity',
position="fill", width=0.5,colour="black") +

geom_bar(aes(colour=Taxon), stat='identity',
position="fill", width=0.5, fill=NA) +
scale_color_manual("",values=c("transparent","red","transparent"))

How's that?

Regards,
Ron.

messages.subject: Re: Change the order how ggplot draws border colors in geom_bar
parts: > I have quite a lot of taxa, so the scale_color_manual argument will be quite tedious to write

All you need is to know how many taxa you have, and where within those B sits (plotting
order-wise; which would be alphabetical by default or something else if you've declared a factor
with levels and labels in a specific order).

Then something like:

outlines <- rep("transparent", number_of_taxa)
outlines[position_of_taxon_B] <- "red"
...
ggplot()+....+scale_colour_manual("", values = outlines)

should do it. I hope.

Ron.

parts:
I don't know if you are still dealing with this, but it sounds like something I had to do recently - I will explain it in terms of my situation, and you can see if it applies to you.

I have a large data frame with data from other the literature, and data from my own research. I wanted to highlight my data in scatter plots and a histogram. 
I added a column to my data frame and called it my.data. For my data I entered "yes" in that column, and everybody else's data got a "no".
In the ggplot function I set fill = my.data, and just had to set two colors in scale_color_manual to have my bars in one color, and all of the other bars another color.

I hope this helps - if not, perhaps it will help somebody else :-) 

~Liz
